pr.title: Do not const prop unions
pr.description:
Unions can produce values whose types don't match their underlying layout types which can lead to ICEs on eval.

Fixes #121534
pr.author: gurry

analysis.originalLogic: KnownPanicsLint's `ConstPropagator` const-propagated every MIR `Aggregate` uniformly: it mapped each aggregate field through `self.eval_operand(field)` (falling back to `Value::Uninit`) and built a `Value::Aggregate`. For `AggregateKind::Adt`, the variant came from the ADT variant index, with arrays, tuples, closures, coroutines, and coroutine closures all assigned `VariantIdx::new(0)`. This treated union aggregates as if their initialized field values could safely be represented by an immediate of the field's type.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation const-propagated union aggregate fields into `Value::Immediate` values and then used those propagated operands in later operations. Union layout interpretation can yield values whose types do not match the underlying layout type: a `u32` field read from a union initialized through an `i32` field can be represented as a negative/signed immediate. That propagated value then reaches `check_binary_op`, which calls `overflowing_binary_op` and triggers the ICE `invalid asymmetric binary op Sub: 4294967294 (i32), 2 (u32)`. The fix does not try to repair the value; it refuses to const-propagate union aggregates at all.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR containing `AggregateKind::Adt` constructions for `union` types whose fields have the same storage size but different semantic/layout interpretation (e.g. `u32` and `i32` fields), especially when values read through one union field are subsequently used in arithmetic with values read through another field. The input must be a union ADT aggregate, identifiable by `Some(_)` in the last tuple position of `AggregateKind::Adt`, rather than an ordinary struct, array, tuple, closure, coroutine, or coroutine-closure aggregate.
analysis.summary: KnownPanicsLint must not const-propagate union aggregate fields. The pass previously evaluated union aggregate operands like ordinary ADT fields; union layout reinterpretation can produce immediates whose types disagree with the underlying layout type, leading to an ICE in binary-op evaluation. The merged fix returns `None` for any `AggregateKind::Adt` whose last field is `Some(_)`, conservatively skipping const propagation for unions.
analysis.trigger: Const-propagating a union aggregate whose initialized/read fields use different types of the same layout size, followed by evaluating an operation on those propagated values. In the linked issue, subtracting a `u32`-read union value from an `i32`-read union value produced `invalid asymmetric binary op Sub: 4294967294 (i32), 2 (u32)`.
preconditions: The MIR contains an `AggregateKind::Adt` for a union, encoded as the last `Option<FieldIdx>` being `Some(_)`.
The union fields can be initialized or read through differing field types that share layout size, such as `u32` and `i32`.
A subsequent operation consumes the const-propagated values, allowing `KnownPanicsLint::check_binary_op` to evaluate the operation.
pitfalls: Do not assume a union field's value has the type of the field used for access; the underlying layout type may differ.
Do not attempt to preserve union const propagation by coercing or normalizing the immediate; the merged fix deliberately returns `None` for union aggregates.
Do not treat the union check as applying to ordinary struct ADTs: only `AggregateKind::Adt(_, _, _, _, Some(_))` indicates a union.
This is const-propagation suppression, not a runtime union-read fix; the conservative `None` means no lint value is produced for that aggregate.
No compiler execution or ICE reproduction was performed here; conclusions are based on the supplied patch and issue text.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a UI regression test under `tests/ui/lint/` with `//@ build-pass` that defines a union with same-sized differently-signed fields, constructs separate union variants through those fields, reads them via the same field type, and performs arithmetic on the results. The merged test uses `union Union { u32_field: u32, i32_field: i32 }`, initializes `u32_variant` with `2` and `i32_variant` with `3`, reads both through `u32_field`, and computes `let _diff = a - b;`. The test specifically guards against an ICE while KnownPanicsLint evaluates an operation whose operands have different layout types even though they have the same type.
